analysis: The PR only changes a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Startup/StartupPreloadTests.swift. It adds one test, `failuresReachFailureHook` (head lines 300-316). The test checks that `deps.onFailure` receives (id, error) for a failed load and a failed self-test, and that a healthy model produces no failure entry. No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage code is modified. I found no change to any asset, trust boundary or mitigation. The T-041 prefix-cache definition was supplied as context; the test touches no cache-storage code. The tests use stub error types and temp files in `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`; they carry no secrets and no network access. One test (`providerPreparationRaceRechecksResidency`) writes a fake HF snapshot into the real default HF cache directory and removes it in a `defer`. This is pre-existing and not part of the change. The new test's `onFailure` hook implies a production `StartupPreloader.Dependencies.onFailure` API. That code is outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that the production hook does not forward raw error text containing sensitive paths or prompt data to external telemetry. I could not verify this from the supplied units, so I recorded it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The base text excerpt (lines 658-1248) and the head text (lines 1-658) are the same test content with only that one addition; I found nothing security-relevant in either.
